title: Used to and would
goal: Talk about old habits, and don’t confuse “used to” with “be used to”
intro: “Used to + verb” describes past habits or states that are no longer true: “I used to live in Kolkata.” It is different from “be used to + -ing”, which means “be familiar with”: “I’m used to working late.” Many learners say “I am used to go” when they mean “I usually go”.

rules.rule: used to + base form = in the past, but not now.
examples: I used to play football every day.
There used to be a cinema here.

rules.rule: Negative and question: didn’t use to / Did you use to…?
examples: I didn’t use to like coffee.
Did you use to live here?

rules.rule: be / get used to + -ing = be familiar with.
examples: She’s getting used to living alone.

rules.rule: For present habits, use “usually”, not “used to”.
examples: I usually go for a walk after dinner.

mistakes.wrong: I am used to go for a walk daily.
mistakes.right: I usually go for a walk every day.

mistakes.wrong: I use to live in Patna.
mistakes.right: I used to live in Patna.

mistakes.wrong: I’m used to wake up early.
mistakes.right: I’m used to waking up early.

ex.q: I ___ in a hostel when I was in college.
I ___ go to the gym on weekends. (now)
It took time, but now I’m used to ___ in the city.
I am used to go to office by metro.
ex.fixed: I usually go to office by metro.

ex.q: She didn't used to eat spicy food.
ex.fixed: She didn't use to eat spicy food.

ex.q: He is getting used to work at night.
ex.fixed: He is getting used to working at night.

ex.q: There ___ to be a big tree in front of our house.

ex.a: I used to be very shy in school.

ex.q: Correct this: “I am used to drink tea every morning.”
a: I usually drink tea every morning

talk: Compare your life ten years ago and now: what you used to do, what you usually do now, and something you are still getting used to.
